    - heading "Accessibility" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: The card is a group labelled by the question; the rows are a listbox with one tab stop that moves with the arrows
      - listitem: Every row says its number key (aria-keyshortcuts); Later says Escape
      - listitem: Answers and Later are announced politely – what you picked and how many still wait
      - listitem: Focus rings show only for the keyboard (:focus-visible); the field for your own words gets no ring, only a firmer edge
      - listitem: After an answer the focus moves to the next decision, the pager arrows keep it while you page, Later moves it to Show and Show back to the row – it never falls back to the page, even when your array drops the decision in focus
      - listitem: "After the last answer the card folds away and can't know your composer: move the focus there yourself in onDecide, e.g. if (open.length === 1) composerRef.current?.focus()"
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: The next decision fades in; after the last answer the card folds away – its height to zero, then gone
      - listitem: Brought up with reveal, the card pulses gray once
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything simply appears
    - heading "Responsive behavior" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: One white card with a hairline edge and a soft lift, no gray layer around it – it takes the width of your composer
      - listitem: Long titles and fact values wrap to a second line, then end in …; summaries and the task stay on one line – nothing leaves the card on phones
      - listitem: One or two tiles keep the size of three; below 420px the tiles turn into rows
      - listitem: On touch screens rows are 44px tall and buttons 32px to see, 40px to hit
      - listitem: "Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme=\"dark\""
    - heading "Notes for AI" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Give your coding assistant this summary instead of screenshots.
    - list:
      - listitem: Put it right above the chat composer, in the same column – the composer stays for new prompts, the card has its own field
      - listitem: Keep options to three to five with a one-line summary each; mark at most one recommended
      - listitem: Remove a decision from the array in onDecide – after the last one the card folds away by itself; then focus the composer
